subject.title: [Feature]: You are spaming ChatGPT like crazy

question: Should main-session cron `systemEvent` reminders get a new literal/simple-reminder bypass, or should deterministic users be expected to move this class of work to command cron?
rationale: Both directions are plausible: bypassing the model reduces cost for simple reminders, but changing `systemEvent` semantics can break cron events that intentionally rely on model reasoning, tools, summarization, or internal-only handling.

options.title: Add a narrow literal reminder mode
options.body: Add an explicit cron payload, flag, or conservative simple-reminder boundary for trusted text that should be delivered without a model call, and document that `systemEvent` remains model-backed.

options.title: Keep command cron as the only no-model path
options.body: Close the product direction by telling users to emit literal stdout from command cron jobs when they need zero-token scheduled delivery.

options.title: Auto-detect simple systemEvents
options.body: Bypass the model when an event looks simple, accepting more ambiguity and higher regression risk around reminders that need reasoning or internal handling.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow literal reminder mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit cron payload, flag, or conservative simple-reminder boundary for trusted text that should be delivered without a model call, and document that `systemEvent` remains model-backed.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter posted the prior keep-open review and has the strongest history signal for the heartbeat event-filter/product-boundary decision.
